prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System (WUI, steep terrain). Baseline: segmentation, time sync, health checks, audit logs; coordination records keep timestamps, participants, radio path. Elements: Caldera Incident Command Portal (Emberhall): common operating picture; produces Crew Staging Pin; triage cases; jurisdictional constraints; marks failed radio route impaired (Orion acknowledges); records assignment packages (objective, validity, confirmation, acknowledgments); in Extended Attack preserves aviation decisions (supervisor, period, reason); flags crew assignments for review when Confirmed Ignition changes perimeter/priority. North Lookout Camera Mast: sends Thermal Spot Snippet. South Lookout Camera Mast: produces Camera Cleaning Log (used by Smoke Classifier Module against lens contamination). Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (Kestrel): Battery Swap Ticket to Drone Pilot Operator; reports readiness/health/recovery before recon release. Drone Tasking Service: builds missions; no flight-release authority; no conflict with Marigold lanes. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (Lantern): detection, recommendations, hazard summary updates; applies Ridge Shadow Mask; may down-weight Smoke Classifier Module (never sole basis for aircraft commitment). MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (Brindle): Wind Shift Bulletin to Redtail. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (Badger): fallback aviation relay. Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console (Marigold): blocks plan release if approvals/airspace/tanker readiness incomplete; Runway Release Note; sends Suppression Drop Receipt after drop recorded, timing checked. East (Retardant Batch Slip) and West Retardant Loading Pumps: status informational only. Crewline Mobile Tablet: acknowledgements; shows objectives, caution areas, division assignment, route, rally point, comms channel; caches staging, marks expired packages unavailable. Actors: County Emergency Liaison (Drone Corridor Permit; view-only). Duty Detection Officer (Orion). Drone Pilot Operator. Air Attack Supervisor (Redtail): authorizes recon/retardant planning; reviews held recommendations (recon/loading/weather conflict with plan), then selects intent in Portal. Tanker Base Manager: resolves batch discrepancies. Helitack Crew Leader: acknowledges aircraft activity before moving crews into drop/recon areas; gets package with aviation constraints, landing zone notes after Redtail approval. Ground assignments omit analytic scores; staging georeferenced. States: Confirmed Ignition; Airspace Restricted; Extended Attack.

New part:
S164: Lantern issues a crew exposure refresh only after the current reconnaissance confidence and weather timing fields are both valid.
S165: Hazards shown to crews include unstable snags, limited access, steep slope exposure, utility conflicts, and escape route degradation.
S166: The MesoWest Weather Fusion Node provides weather-derived exposure flags that support staging decisions near ridgelines and drainages.
S167: When the system enters the Airspace Restricted State, helitack assignments show the restriction boundary and require confirmation before aircraft-dependent movement is planned.
S168: The Drone Tasking Service maintains reconnaissance task status so that ground teams can see whether requested intelligence is pending, active, or complete.
S169: Horizon Ridge Drone Dock status is shown as an availability input only and does not by itself authorize crew movement into a new area.
S170: The Drone Pilot Operator confirms launch readiness separately from crew assignment acceptance to keep reconnaissance execution independent from ground deployment.
S171: The VHF Radio Gateway Repeater mirrors priority assignment summaries for crews that cannot maintain a data session in canyon or timbered terrain.
S172: If the data link is degraded, the Crewline Mobile Tablet presents the last verified assignment package and clearly identifies the time of last update.
S173: The Helitack Crew Leader acknowledges assignment receipt, reports readiness, and records any exception that prevents safe execution.
S174: The County Emergency Liaison can view staging posture and public safety implications without gaining authority to alter crew assignments or hazard records.
S175: All assignment and staging changes preserve an audit trail so that later reviews can reconstruct what information was available to each crew at the time of action.
S176: During prolonged wildfire operations, the system shall favor continuity of command decisions over full automation when communications, power, or sensor coverage is impaired.
S177: The Caldera Incident Command Portal enters a disconnected operating mode when its primary network path is unavailable and clearly marks all displayed information with the last synchronization time.
S178: In disconnected operating mode, the Caldera Incident Command Portal allows authorized users to review cached incident data and create queued updates, but it prevents irreversible releases until connectivity is restored.
S179: The Duty Detection Officer receives a visible warning whenever a detection, assignment, or hazard record is based on stale data or partial sensor coverage.
S180: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine shall continue using the last approved model configuration after a repository outage and shall reject unversioned rules or unsigned analytic packages.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
